draft.briefing: Hey, you're at Marari Beach! It's a quiet fishing beach, where wooden boats still head out at dawn. Mararikulam village behind it is lined with coconut palms and coir makers.
draft.hungryLine: Marari eats fish from the morning catch. Ask a homestay or beach shack what came in.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Watch the boats come in at dawn, then cycle through the village lanes.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Lie under the palms and let the day go slowly. That's what Marari is for.
moodReplies.surprise-me: The Mararikulam Mahadeva temple is said to be over a thousand years old.

legends.title: A beach for fishers
legends.body: Marari is a working beach first. Give the fishermen room when they haul in the nets.

legends.title: Rope from a husk
legends.body: Women in these villages soak coconut husks for months, then beat and spin them into rope.

tips.title: Go at dawn.
tips.body: That's when the boats come in and the light is best.

story.title: Coconut coast
story.body: This coast has lived on fishing and coconuts for centuries.

story.title: The temple
story.body: The Mahadeva temple became the heart of the village.

story.title: Coir
story.body: Coir spinning spread through the villages and became a main source of work.

story.title: Quiet travel
story.body: Small homestays and resorts brought travellers looking for a calmer beach.

story.title: Your turn
story.body: Dawn boats, a cycle through the village, then the hammock. Tell me how many boats you counted.

food.name: Beach shacks at Marari
food.detail: Fresh fish fry · ₹₹ · on the beach
